title: Rohingya still await accountability, Guterres says before ICJ ruling
excerpt: The UN chief told the ASEAN-UN Summit that states must protect people fleeing persecution. The world court rules on Myanmar on 19 November.

image.alt: A wide view of bamboo and tarpaulin shelters across Kutupalong refugee camp in Cox's Bazar
image.credit: John Owens (VOA) / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain

content:
UN Secretary-General António Guterres has said the Rohingya "still await accountability for grave violations" nearly a decade after their forced mass displacement from Myanmar, UN News reported on 16 November. He was speaking at the ASEAN-United Nations Summit in Manila.

Guterres said states have a duty to protect people fleeing violence until the conditions for a safe return are in place. "Until these conditions are met, States have a duty to protect those fleeing violence and persecution," he said. UN News put the number of Rohingya living in the camps in Bangladesh at nearly 1.2 million.

His remarks came three days before the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is due to give its judgment in The Gambia's genocide case against Myanmar on 19 November, as Devlens reported from the court's announcement.

Why it matters

For agencies working in Cox's Bazar and Bhasan Char, the ruling and the UN's public line on accountability shape the case for keeping refugees protected and funded while return remains impossible. As Devlens reported, food rations are funded only until April 2027. A clear statement from the UN chief gives NGOs a reference point for advocacy with donors and ASEAN governments.

What to watch

The ICJ judgment on 19 November, how Myanmar and ASEAN members respond, and whether donors link the ruling to new funding for the Rohingya response.
